text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card and tools: 39.3% vs 10.2% expected, 7 of 13 below billed, 0% peer rate, 2 of 24 no-lab, and the $2,300 estimate with CI. Next steps are concrete and citations are real. But the added narrative has an unsupported claim and a framing problem, and the examples do not balance the pattern.","problems":["The claim \"about 2x the peer share at every complexity level\" is not on the card. The by_complexity table gives provider share vs all_provider_share, which ranges from about 1.3x to 8.5x (e.g., 0.154 vs 0.018; 0.496 vs 0.217 is 2.3x; 0.364 vs 0.105 is 3.5x), so \"2x at every level\" is inaccurate.","\"Over half the sampled 99215 charts support only moderate MDM\" overstates a sample of 13 charts, 7 of them below billed. The cautious \"reason to review, not a finding\" sentence from the draft was removed.","\"The sick panel explains some of the excess but not what the charts show\" is an interpretive conclusion that is not backed by the evidence. It also sits awkwardly beside the headline.","\"Random sample of 30 is complete\" is grounded in the tool output, but the summary does not note that only 13 documented 99215 claims support the headline rate, which is a small base.","Low-complexity examples C0034781 and C0034821 have 0 conditions but are not in the documented set, so no chart evidence backs them. C0034848 is similarly unreviewed. The summary does not say these are claims-based examples and not chart-based, so a reader may mix the two kinds of evidence.","The summary does not mention that C0034892 (low complexity, documented moderate, 38 min) was a stronger example combining both signals.","Some rationale sentences are redundant, and the headline and rationale repeat the figures with no new content."]}
